name: GovRAMP (formerly StateRAMP)
purpose: One cloud security verification that state and local governments can share, modeled on FedRAMP.
what: A nonprofit, renamed from StateRAMP in February 2025. Four verified statuses, Core, Ready, Provisional and Authorized, on SP 800-53 Revision 5 at Low, Moderate or High.

binds.line: A membership nonprofit, not a law. Its site lists 72 participating government organizations.

verifiedBy.line: A third-party assessor assesses Ready and Authorized, the program office validates, and a government sponsor or the Approvals Committee approves Authorized.

sits.line: Layer 5. It verifies cloud products against selections from SP 800-53.

verification.note: Read on 14 November 2026, with https://govramp.org/authorized: the statuses are Core, Ready, Provisional and Authorized, on NIST SP 800-53 Revision 5 at a Low, Moderate or High impact level. Authorized needs a security assessment report from a third-party assessor and ‘Government sponsorship or approval through the GovRAMP Approvals Committee’.
Read on 14 November 2026: the rebrand was announced on 14 February 2025. StateRAMP remains the legal name.

Read on 14 November 2026: ‘GovRAMP operates as a 501(c)(6) nonprofit organization governed by a Board of Directors composed primarily of state and local government officials.’ The participating governments page (https://govramp.org/participating-government-organizations) printed 72 that day; the home page says 70+.

terms.line: GovRAMP’s own material. Lensatic describes the program in its own words and links to GovRAMP’s pages.

related.line: GovRAMP’s Fast Track reuses FedRAMP packages, and FedRAMP’s Class A rules accept a GovRAMP assessment.
GovRAMP publishes an overlay aligned to the CJIS Security Policy.
Its baselines select from SP 800-53 Revision 5.
